prompt: In a triangular garden bed, one side is extended past a corner to form an exterior angle. The two interior angles at the OTHER two corners measure $50^\circ$ and $60^\circ$. What is the measure of that exterior angle, in degrees?
hint: An exterior angle is related to the two interior angles far away from it.

hints.text: An exterior angle is related to the two interior angles far away from it.
The Exterior Angle Theorem: the exterior angle equals the SUM of the two remote interior angles.

explanation: The Exterior Angle Theorem says an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote (non-adjacent) interior angles.
The remote interior angles here are $50^\circ$ and $60^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: The long way around
steps: The exterior angle forms a linear pair with it: $180 - 70 = 110^\circ$. Same answer, one step longer — which is why the shortcut theorem exists.
